name: Lucrecia Dalt
label: RVNG Intl.
lede: Lucrecia Dalt started as a Colombian soil engineer with a side hobby in electronics and ended up a Berlin voice artist. In 2022 she made a Spanish-language bolero record about an alien, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 8 of the year.

eras.title: A soil engineer with a maraca
eras.text: She grows up in Pereira, trains as a civil engineer and makes electronic music in Medellín on the side. Her first records come out through Colombian labels and the Series collective, under the name Lucrecia.

years.src: Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · Digital in Berlin: Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: Maracas at four, in Pereira
years.p: Her grandfather played drums and maracas, and her mother played her bambucos, pasillos, boleros and Spanish ballads.
years.xp:
Dalt says her grandfather taught her to play maracas when she was four, and that her mother exposed her to Colombian folk forms: bambucos, pasillos, currulaos, guabinas, boleros.

People often say she's from Medellín. "I was actually born in Pereira," she told Chain DLK, calling the Medellín story a myth, since she lived there for eight years.

The boleros come back two decades later as the rhythmic spine of ¡Ay!.

years.big: "we were trying to skip on all the Vallenato played at the bars and create our own universe"
years.src: Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt · Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · Subbacultcha: An Interview with Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: Soil by day, electronics at night
years.p: Dalt studies civil engineering and works on soil and construction problems in Medellín, and starts making music around 2004. That's her on the Series Media collective, quoted by Chain DLK.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia she spent two years at a geotechnical company in Medellín. Chain DLK puts her in Medellín for eight years before she left for Europe. Series Media, the electronic collective she was close to, put out her first records.

On the engineering, she told Subbacultcha: "I was puzzled about what I could do with all the information I learned, as it was such a big dedication."

years.h: Acerca, signed just "Lucrecia"
years.p: Mil Records puts out her first album, and Series issues a re-edit the same year.

years.h: Still just Lucrecia, on Like Being Home
years.p: The EP is her second release on the Colombian collective, before she takes her full name.

eras.title: A MySpace page, a Berlin label, a ticket out
eras.text: Gudrun Gut hears her online, Dalt leaves Colombia for Barcelona and later Berlin, and Human Ear Music puts out two albums. Julia Holter takes her on tour.

years.src: Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: Gudrun Gut finds her on MySpace
years.p: Asked by Chain DLK why she moved to Europe, Dalt gave one word. Gut, the Berlin producer, had contacted her for the compilation 4 Women No Cry on Monika Enterprise.
years.xp:
Chain DLK reports that Dalt was discovered through MySpace by [[Gudrun Gut|22e67027-3c07-44d5-8501-8eed7b13286b]], which led to 4 Women No Cry in 2008. "Gudrun Gut contacted me through MySpace," Dalt confirmed. The same compilation is where she met [[Julia Holter|45610c1f-41a4-44f1-9da6-227510073ffc]].

She lived in Barcelona before settling in Berlin.

years.h: Congost lands on Pruna
years.p: Pruna Recordings releases it the year after the 4 Women No Cry compilation.

years.h: Commotus opens the Human Ear Music run
years.p: It's her first album on the label; Syzygy follows in 2013.

years.h: A year later, Syzygy
years.p: Human Ear Music releases her second album for the label, 12 months after Commotus.

years.h: [[Julia Holter|45610c1f-41a4-44f1-9da6-227510073ffc]] takes her on the road in Europe
years.p: The two had met through the 4 Women No Cry compilation. The tour starts October 24.

years.src: CLOT: Lucrecia Dalt, earthly encounters · Crack Magazine: The phantasmagoric poetics of Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: A long collaboration with [[Regina de Miguel|2f203b06-7d52-486c-9605-c653e4276613]] begins
years.p: The pair have worked together since 2014 on the politics of listening, including the audiovisual mystic opera V.I.T.R.I.O.L.. The same year she puts out a self-titled EP on [[Nicolás Jaar|06e99a1b-4020-4380-ab27-1a3e0c5e557c]]'s Other People.

years.h: Ou goes to Care Of Editions
years.p: The imprint also released a Dalt 12-inch around the same time.

eras.title: The voice takes over
eras.text: On RVNG Intl. she cuts everything back to synths and her own processed voice. Two albums in two years, then noise collaborations on the side.

years.cap: Dalt live at Electro-Mechanica, St Petersburg, November 3, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Anticlines (album) · CLOT: Lucrecia Dalt, earthly encounters
years.h: Every sound on Anticlines is her voice or a synth, Dalt says
years.p: RVNG Intl. releases it, and Pitchfork gives it 8.0.
years.xp:
She built it mainly on a Nord Modular and a Moogerfooger MuRF, with lyrics co-written with Henry Anderson. Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne singled out its vocal dimension, including spoken-word passages with subtle processing.

Videos followed for "Edge" and "Tar".

years.cap: Dalt live at Electro-Mechanica, St Petersburg
years.src: Wikipedia: No Era Sólida · Crack Magazine: The phantasmagoric poetics of Lucrecia Dalt · Subbacultcha: An Interview with Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: No Era Sólida borrows a character from Ballard and Lispector
years.p: Dalt records and mixes it herself in Berlin, at INA GRM in Paris and at Pioneer Works in Brooklyn. Pitchfork gives it 7.9.
years.xp:
The album follows a fictional character, Lia, drawn from a J.G. Ballard short story and Clarice Lispector's novel A Breath of Life. Part of the sales went to Tierra Digna, which supports Colombian communities.

She has said the first song was a complete improvisation. Before it, she told Subbacultcha, "I would listen to singers in languages I don't know for hours."

years.h: Aaron Dilloway and Dalt make Lucy and Aaron
years.p: The Hanson release comes with two EPs, Demands of Ordinary Devotion and The Blob, made with the former [[Wolf Eyes|51ff6576-95ff-4e02-a0cf-fad3b39c0b8d]] member on his label.

eras.title: Preta lands
eras.text: An alien in a bought human body, and a Spanish-language bolero record. It's the year Dalt goes from quiet favorite to critics' favorite, and she scores a horror film and an HBO series too.

years.src: Spitfire Audio: Lucrecia Dalt talks loud scores
years.h: Sam Walker's The Seed and HBO's The Baby both get Dalt scores
years.p: The Seed is her first film score, for Walker's horror film. The The Baby score follows, and both come out on Invada.
years.xp:
For The Baby she recorded herself, her partner and drummer Alex Lázaro, vocalist Audrey Chen and Canadian throat singer Cynthia Pitsiulak on ribbon microphones.

"When I find directors who want to have the score present and loud," she told Spitfire Audio, "that is pure joy for me."

years.h: "No Tiempo" comes with a short film by Aina Climent
years.p: The lead single from ¡Ay! opens on a sustained organ chord.
years.xp: The FADER made it a Song You Need on July 19, calling out the organ chord that unwinds into an orchestral arrangement.

q: Her mission is to create an anomaly on earth so humans can experience 'no time', which is her permanent state.
years.src: Subbacultcha: An Interview with Lucrecia Dalt · The FADER: Song You Need · Wikipedia: ¡Ay!
years.h: Preta buys a body in a hydrosphere market
years.p: Dalt and philosopher Miguel Prado write the script for ¡Ay!: an alien buys a human body and frets over humans' obsession with time.
years.xp:
The album is sung entirely in Spanish and leans on bolero-shaped rhythms, played on acoustic instruments. Dalt describes "Atemporal" as a collection of Dalts from different eras, with vocoders, synths and processed drums.

Videos also went out for "Dicen" and "Enviada".

years.h: ¡Ay! lands at No. 8 on Pitchfork's year-end list
years.p: RVNG Intl. releases the 10-song, 34-minute album. Pitchfork scores it 8.6, and Metacritic lists it at 83.
years.xp:
Trumpeter Lina Allemano, clarinetist Edith Steyer, bassists Nick Dunston and Isabel Rößler and percussionist Alex Lázaro play on it, and Marta Salogni mixed it. It's her first solo release since No Era Sólida.

The Washington Post called it "a richly percussive, luxuriously spacious recording", per Wikipedia's reception section.

years.h: The Wire puts ¡Ay! at the top of 2022
years.p: Its Releases of the Year list ranks the album No. 1.

eras.title: A Danger to Ourselves
eras.text: David Sylvian co-produces, another soundtrack follows, and Dalt makes a stranger, pop-adjacent record after Preta.

years.h: David Sylvian co-produces A Danger to Ourselves
years.p: Fourteen tracks on RVNG Intl., with [[Juana Molina|eca5dd0e-edc7-4658-85f0-762e263b4acd]] guesting; "Cosa Rara" came out in January and "Divina" in May.
years.xp: The Skinny gave it five stars. Clash gave it 8/10 and called it "something strange and eerie, yet surprisingly close to a pop album".

years.h: Another score, Rabbit Trap, on Invada
years.p: It joins The Seed and The Baby on the label. She also puts out the Caes EP on RVNG Intl.
